text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after birth. To begin my assessment, when did the seizures first start, and have you noticed any fever, poor feeding, or difficulty breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of seizures, lethargy, and low birth weight in the context of antenatal chorioamnionitis is highly concerning for neonatal sepsis and meningitis. Given the poor Apgar scores and rapid deterioration, I need to confirm the presence of infection. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Blood Culture, and Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) analysis including Gram stain and culture.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis with Meningitis

The findings of a tense anterior fontanelle, sluggish pupils, irregular breathing, and slow eye movements strongly suggest intracranial infection and increased intracranial pressure rather than isolated pneumonia. I am proceeding with the CSF analysis and cultures I ordered to confirm this.
